chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Jameel, from Ismail Al Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The divorce of a pregnant woman is one (revocation). So when she places what is in her belly, she has been irrevocably divorced from him.
ai.seo_question: How many times is a pregnant woman considered divorced according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a pregnant woman’s iddah extends until childbirth, a ruling derived from the principle that the womb is the primary indicator of her state. It establishes that the divorce is irrevocable (ba'in) upon delivery, distinguishing this specific case from the standard three-month waiting period for non-pregnant women. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the finality of talaq and the woman's eligibility for remarriage.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Jameel, from Ismail Al Ju’fy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Divorce of a pregnant woman is once. So when she places what is in her belly, so she has been irrevocably divorced from him’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn abu Nasr from Jamil from ’Isma‘il al-Ju‘fiy who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Divorce of a pregnant woman is one and when she gives birth she become stranger to him.’”
